name: manila-1899
title: Manila, February 1899: reconstructed base map (WarMapper)
note: A WarMapper reconstruction, not a period map. Features were read from two 1899 Army maps; see pipeline/recon/manila_1899.py. [longitude, latitude], WGS 84.

properties.desc: Bay shore from the Vitas canal mouth to the north mole of the Pasig
properties.basis: Read from gridded crops of the engineer map (3,840-px copy), 3 to 6 scan px a pick (10-25 m).

properties.desc: Bay shore from the south side of the Pasig mouth to Malate
properties.basis: Read from gridded crops of the engineer map (3,840-px copy), 3 to 6 scan px a pick (10-25 m).

properties.desc: Outer shore north of the Vitas canal, to the Navotas spit
properties.basis: Read from the Signal Corps map (full scan, crops at half size); placed by that map's own fit (about 170 m) and slid to meet the engineer map's line. Slid 8 m. The outer edge of the Dagat-Dagatan lagoons and the Navotas sand spit; the map is schematic here.

properties.desc: Bay shore from Malate past the fort on the beach to Pasay
properties.basis: Read from crops of "Manila y sus arrabales" (War Department, 1898; 4,551 x 7,118 scan) and checked by laying the picks back on the scan. Placed by that sheet's fit to the engineer map; south of Malate, where the sheet is a hand-drawn strip, slid to today's F. B. Harrison Street crossings as well (pipeline/georef/manila_arrabales_fit.py). The shore is that of 1898.

properties.desc: Bay shore south of Pasay, towards Paranaque
properties.basis: Read from the Signal Corps map (full scan, crops at half size); placed by that map's own fit (about 170 m) and slid to meet the engineer map's line. Slid 236 m to meet the shore of the 1898 sheet west of Pasay.

properties.name: Manila Bay
properties.basis: The area west of the traced shoreline, out to the edge of the sheet. Its landward edge is the shore layers; the other edges are the sheet's.

properties.name: Jetty
properties.desc: The long jetty south of the river mouth, from the light at its head
properties.basis: Read from gridded crops of the engineer map (3,840-px copy), 3 to 6 scan px a pick (10-25 m).

properties.desc: North mole of the Pasig mouth

properties.name: Pasig River
properties.basis: The blue water tint of the engineer map, separated by colour inside the inked bank lines and vectorised (about 4 m a pixel); gaps under lettering closed and three leaks cut by hand. The island below Malacanang is left as land. The outline stops at the mole heads and at the sheet's south edge.

properties.name: Pasig River
properties.desc: The Pasig above Santa Ana, past San Pedro Macati
properties.basis: Read from the Signal Corps map (full scan, crops at half size); placed by that map's own fit (about 170 m) and slid to meet the engineer map's line. Slid 140 m. A centre line only: the width is taken from the engineer map where the two meet.

properties.name: San Juan River
properties.basis: Read from gridded crops of the engineer map (3,840-px copy), 3 to 6 scan px a pick (10-25 m). Centre line; the map draws it about 30 m wide.

properties.desc: Streets, blocks, dykes and field lines: Caloocan, La Loma, Lico and the country north of the city
properties.basis: Every dark ink line of the engineer map inside this part of the sheet, separated from the scan by a program, thinned to centre lines and vectorised (about 2 m), then placed by the map's fit. Small separate marks (most lettering, the dots of trails, hedge rings) were dropped by size. Nobody has checked it line by line: it holds street and block edges, dykes, fences, banks and hachures, and also what the program cannot tell from them, such as letters that touch a line and field works drawn after 4 February.
properties.part: Caloocan, La Loma, Lico and the country north of the city

properties.desc: Roads, field lines, marsh and old works: Malate, Singalong and the strip to Pasay
properties.basis: Every dark ink line of the 1898 sheet south of where the engineer map stops, separated from the scan by a program, thinned and vectorised, then placed as the shore of this layer's map is. It holds roads, field lines, the estero and marsh behind Malate, the old Spanish line of works by blockhouses 13 and 14, and the trenches the Americans dug in August 1898. Nobody has checked it line by line, and it is the ground of 1898, six months before the battle.

properties.name: Calle Real
properties.desc: Calle Real from the fort at Malate to the road to Pasay church
properties.basis: Read from crops of "Manila y sus arrabales" (War Department, 1898; 4,551 x 7,118 scan) and checked by laying the picks back on the scan. Placed by that sheet's fit to the engineer map; south of Malate, where the sheet is a hand-drawn strip, slid to today's F. B. Harrison Street crossings as well (pipeline/georef/manila_arrabales_fit.py). The shore is that of 1898. The road drawn as a double line nearest the shore; the sheet letters it "Calle Real" in Malate.

properties.name: Blockhouse 13
properties.basis: A work on the old Spanish line of the 1898 sheet with "13" written beside it in pencil by an unknown hand; taken to be blockhouse 13. Placed as the shore of this map is.

properties.name: Blockhouse 14
properties.basis: A work on the old Spanish line of the 1898 sheet with "14" written beside it in pencil by an unknown hand; taken to be blockhouse 14. Placed as the shore of this map is.

properties.desc: Works north of the Kansas line of 5 to 10 February, by the railway (three humps)
properties.basis: The legend's mark for insurgent works (a row of humps), read from a crop of the engineer map at three times its size, 3 to 5 scan px a pick. Short pieces only: the map shows them by blockhouses 1 and 2 and nowhere else on the sheet. Those south of the American line of 5 to 10 February were Filipino works facing the city before the battle.
